opts: Hyperthermia and shivering with nausea and vomiting; contraindicated with a scarred uterus
Hypertension and headache; contraindicated in established maternal heart disease
Bronchospasm, since misoprostol provokes an attack in asthmatic women
Profuse watery diarrhoea; contraindicated in maternal pulmonary hypertension
exp: Misoprostol causes fever, shivering and gastrointestinal upset; unlike carboprost it is safe in asthma but risky with a uterine scar.

opts: The vagina just below the urethra, presenting as suburethral nodules
The liver, presenting months later with obstructive jaundice
The brain, presenting with seizures and focal neurological deficits
The pelvis, presenting with deep pelvic pain and a palpable mass
exp: After the lungs, the vagina is the second commonest site: suburethral nodules that may bleed are the classic presentation.

opts: Hold the baby's back and rotate the shoulders into the antero-posterior diameter, then await spontaneous delivery
Perform Lovset's manoeuvre immediately without first rotating the shoulders
Apply fundal pressure to push the shoulders down through the pelvic brim
Apply Piper's forceps to deliver the head before the shoulders are released
exp: If the shoulders are not in the antero-posterior diameter, rotate them there first; only if that fails move to Lovset's manoeuvre.

opts: Fibrinogen, factors VII, VIII, IX and X, and von Willebrand factor
Only factor XI and factor XIII, both of which also rise markedly
Antithrombin III and protein S, the natural anticoagulants
Tissue plasminogen activator, which keeps the maternal circulation fluid
exp: Clotting factors and fibrinogen rise, while antithrombin and protein S fall — which is why pregnancy is prothrombotic.

opts: Asthma, pulmonary hypertension and suspected amniotic fluid embolism; dinoprostone is used off-label
Heart disease and Rh-negative status, with dinoprostone as the first-line drug
A scarred uterus only, with dinoprostone as the accepted gold standard
Diabetes mellitus, with dinoprostone given by intravenous infusion
exp: Carboprost is contraindicated in asthma and pulmonary hypertension; dinoprostone (PGE2) is used off-label per vaginam or rectum.

opts: From the sacro-iliac joint on one side to the iliopectineal eminence on the other
From one ischial spine straight across to the ischial spine opposite
From the symphysis pubis directly backwards to the sacral promontory
From one ischial tuberosity across to the opposite tuberosity
exp: The oblique diameters run from a sacro-iliac joint to the opposite iliopectineal eminence and measure about 12 cm.

opts: Painless bleeding alone, with no systemic upset whatsoever
No systemic symptoms ever, because the infection stays localised
Fever and chills, abdominal pain, vomiting and a purulent vaginal discharge
Palmar pruritus, which is the only symptom that reliably appears
exp: Septic abortion is a spreading infection: fever and chills, abdominal pain, gastrointestinal upset and purulent discharge.

opts: 100 microgram slowly intravenously; half-life 40 minutes; not used for induction or for treating PPH
250 microgram intramuscularly; half-life 5 minutes; used to treat PPH
10 IU intramuscularly; half-life 20 minutes; used for induction of labour
1 mg intravenously; half-life 60 minutes; the standard treatment for PPH
exp: Carbetocin is a long-acting oxytocin analogue given as 100 microgram for prevention at caesarean, not for induction or PPH treatment.

opts: About 80 mL more cord blood reaching the baby, giving extra iron and less neonatal anaemia
Prevention of postpartum haemorrhage in the mother after delivery
A lower risk of neonatal jaundice needing treatment with phototherapy
Prevention of retained placenta in the third stage of labour
exp: Delayed clamping transfers about 80 mL more blood, roughly 50 mg of elemental iron, and reduces infant anaemia; it slightly increases jaundice.

opts: Two placentas, or one that appears single, with the twin peak or lambda sign
A single placenta with a T sign at the membrane insertion
A single placenta with no distinguishing ultrasound sign at all
Two separate placentas but with a T sign between the membranes
exp: Dichorionic twins have two placentas, or a fused single-looking one, and always show the lambda or twin-peak sign.

opts: About 25% at 28 weeks, 5% at 34 weeks and 3-4% at term, as most turn spontaneously
About 3-4% at 28 weeks, 5% at 34 weeks and 25% at term, as more turn with time
About 50% at 28 weeks, 25% at 34 weeks and 10% at term in most series
About 10% at 28 weeks, 3% at 34 weeks and 1% at term after routine version
exp: Breech is common early and uncommon at term because most babies turn by themselves as gestation advances.

opts: Amniocentesis with Gram stain, culture and histology of the fetal membranes
Clinical criteria alone, which are sensitive and specific enough on their own
A raised maternal C-reactive protein measured on admission in labour
Ultrasound findings of debris and a thickened placenta
exp: Clinical criteria make a presumptive diagnosis; definitive diagnosis needs amniotic fluid studies and membrane histology.

opts: Ectopic pregnancy uses a single full dose in one day; GTN uses multi-dose therapy with folinic acid
Both conditions always use exactly the same methotrexate regimen
Ectopic pregnancy is treated with folinic acid alone, never with methotrexate
Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is never treated with methotrexate
exp: The ectopic regimen is a single dose with day 4 and day 7 hCG checks, whereas GTN regimens use repeated doses alternated with folinic acid rescue.

q: Management protocol for protracted active phase begins with vaginal examination — match the finding to the action: cephalopelvic disproportion : occipito-posterior position : inadequate contractions.
opts: CPD: caesarean section — occipito-posterior: wait for spontaneous rotation — inadequate contractions: assess them abdominally
CPD: wait and observe — occipito-posterior: caesarean section — inadequate contractions: start oxytocin
CPD: start oxytocin — occipito-posterior: caesarean section — inadequate contractions: wait and observe
CPD: amniotomy — occipito-posterior: forceps delivery — inadequate contractions: caesarean section
exp: The finding on examination decides the action: disproportion is delivered, a good pelvis with malposition is given time, and weak contractions are assessed then augmented.

opts: Consumptive coagulopathy, from abruption, amniotic fluid embolism, septic abortion, acute fatty liver and prolonged fetal death
Consumptive coagulopathy, caused by placenta previa and nothing else
Dilutional coagulopathy, caused by postpartum haemorrhage alone
A hypercoagulable state, caused by maternal sepsis alone
exp: Obstetric DIC is consumptive: thromboplastin or tissue factor enters the circulation and consumes fibrinogen and platelets.

opts: Manual removal under anaesthesia, sweeping the hand in the plane between the uterus and the placenta
Wait one hour for spontaneous expulsion before any intervention
An oxytocin bolus combined with firm fundal pressure
Emergency hysterectomy, since the cord can no longer be secured
exp: Once the cord snaps, controlled traction is impossible, so the placenta is removed manually in the correct plane under anaesthesia.

opts: Only until the seizure stops, after which the magnesium is discontinued
For seven days after delivery, to cover the late risk of seizures
Until 20 weeks of gestation in cases of early severe disease
Until 24 hours after delivery or 24 hours after the last convulsion, whichever is later
exp: Maintenance continues for 24 hours after delivery or 24 hours after the last convulsion, whichever comes later.

opts: Piper's: the longest forceps, for the after-coming head — Tucker-McLane: the only forceps with a solid blade
Piper's: a solid blade for the head — Tucker-McLane: for the after-coming head
Piper's: a short outlet forceps — Tucker-McLane: the rotational forceps
Piper's: a sliding lock — Tucker-McLane: the shortest forceps available
exp: Piper's are long forceps with a perineal curve for the after-coming head; Tucker-McLane are the only forceps with solid blades.

opts: Shock with little visible bleeding; from a cervical or vaginal tear extending upwards
Heavy vaginal bleeding from uterine atony after the delivery
Fever and pelvic pain from puerperal endometritis
A visible vulval swelling from a torn pudendal artery
exp: A supralevator collection is occult: shock out of proportion to visible loss, from an upward extension of a cervical or vaginal tear.

q: Postnatal visits — ACOG recommendation : Government of India recommendation.
opts: ACOG: an initial visit at 3 weeks and a final visit at 12 weeks — GOI: day 1, day 3, day 7 and 6 weeks
ACOG: day 1 and 6 weeks only — GOI: visits at 3 weeks and 12 weeks
ACOG: visits at 2, 4 and 6 weeks — GOI: day 1, day 7 and day 42
ACOG: a single visit on day 7 — GOI: a single visit at 6 weeks
exp: ACOG restructures postnatal care as an ongoing process with a contact by 3 weeks and a comprehensive visit by 12 weeks; India schedules four early visits.

opts: Caesarean section, since vaginal delivery is contraindicated, and it commits her to repeat sections
A trial of labour is always attempted first, whatever the degree of contraction
Instrumental delivery once the cervix has reached full dilatation
Induction of labour with oxytocin from 38 completed weeks onwards
exp: A genuinely contracted pelvis precludes vaginal delivery, and the indication recurs in every subsequent pregnancy.

opts: Non-compliance from gastrointestinal side effects, which blackening of the stool can confirm
Severe intestinal malabsorption, demonstrated by a negative stool test
Bone marrow aplasia, which should always be excluded by aspiration
Excessive urinary excretion of iron, measured in a 24-hour collection
exp: The commonest reason is that she has stopped taking it because of nausea or constipation; asking about black stools is a simple objective check.

opts: A normal cervix on transvaginal scan with no history of any pregnancy loss
Maternal age above forty alone, even with no previous pregnancy loss
At least two painless second-trimester losses, irrespective of the scan findings
Any single first-trimester loss, since one loss reliably predicts another
exp: A history-based indication is recurrent painless mid-trimester loss, typically two or more, and it applies whatever the cervical length shows.

opts: Both are listed for early preterm labour and both again for late preterm labour
Only in early preterm labour, since late preterm labour needs neither
Only in late preterm labour, since early delivery is already inevitable
In neither group, since both are given only after 37 completed weeks
exp: In the summary table corticosteroids and GBS screening appear in both the early and the late preterm labour columns.

opts: 600 microgram orally or sublingually, within a range of 400 to 600 microgram
25 microgram vaginally, repeated every six hours as required
800 microgram rectally, which is the WHO recommended single dose
200 microgram orally, which is the maximum dose the mother tolerates
exp: In active management misoprostol is used where oxytocin is unavailable, in a dose of 400-600 microgram orally or sublingually.

opts: Prolonged second stage, fetal distress, and shortening the second stage for maternal disease
A prolonged first stage, and cephalopelvic disproportion in established labour
Breech presentation, and a transverse lie with the arm prolapsed
Placenta previa, and cord prolapse with the cervix only 4 cm dilated
exp: Instrumental delivery is for the second stage: delay, fetal distress, or a maternal indication to avoid pushing.

opts: Hypoplasia of the nasal bridge, stippled epiphyses and central nervous system abnormalities
Phocomelia, amelia and ano-rectal atresia in the affected infant
Ebstein anomaly, fetal goitre and bilateral renal agenesis
Cleft lip, cleft palate and postaxial polydactyly
exp: DiSaia syndrome is warfarin embryopathy: nasal hypoplasia, chondrodysplasia punctata and central nervous system defects.

opts: Ambulation, oral intake, pain relief and a companion of the woman's choice
Pain relief alone, since the others are obstetric interventions
Bladder care and fetal monitoring, which together define supportive care
An enema and perineal shaving, as recommended routinely on admission
exp: Supportive care bundles the low-technology measures: mobility, fluids, analgesia and continuous support.

opts: Breech and transverse lie, with ultrasound confirming lie, liquor, singleton pregnancy and no gross anomaly
Face and brow presentation, with ultrasound assessing the placenta alone
Twin pregnancy, with ultrasound determining chorionicity and amnionicity
Occipito-posterior position, with ultrasound measuring the biparietal diameter
exp: Version is offered for breech and transverse lie after ultrasound confirms the lie, adequate liquor, a singleton and no major anomaly.

opts: Oligohydramnios below 5 cm, and polyhydramnios at 25 cm or more
Oligohydramnios below 2 cm, and polyhydramnios above 8 cm
Oligohydramnios below 10 cm, and polyhydramnios at 35 cm or more
Oligohydramnios below 1 cm, and polyhydramnios at 15 cm or more
exp: By amniotic fluid index, oligohydramnios is below 5 cm and polyhydramnios is 25 cm or more; the 2 cm and 8 cm values belong to the deepest pocket method.

opts: A day-7 fall of less than 15% after three doses, or a rising hCG from day 4 to day 7
Any rise at all in the hCG measured on day 1 after the first injection
A fall of exactly 15% between the day 4 and the day 7 measurements
The absence of vaginal bleeding on the first day of treatment
exp: Treatment is judged to have failed after three doses if the day-7 fall is under 15%, or if the hCG is still rising between days 4 and 7.

opts: A blood-stained mucus show in preterm labour, which is not antepartum haemorrhage
Bleeding from placental abruption with a tender, contracting uterus
Painless recurrent bleeding from placenta previa in the third trimester
Bleeding from vasa previa accompanied by fetal bradycardia
exp: A show is mucus with a little blood from the cervix; antepartum haemorrhage means bleeding from the placental site or vessels after viability.

opts: At least three in 10 minutes, each lasting 45 seconds and raising pressure by 65-75 mmHg
At least five in 10 minutes, each lasting 60 seconds at 100 mmHg
At least two in 10 minutes, each lasting 20 seconds at 30 mmHg
At least three in 15 minutes, each lasting 30 seconds at 50 mmHg
exp: Adequate contractions are three or more in ten minutes, each lasting about 45 seconds with an amplitude of 65-75 mmHg.

opts: The need for neonatal resuscitation, as in birth asphyxia
An Rh-negative mother, to limit feto-maternal transfusion
Maternal HIV infection, to reduce the risk of viral transmission
Preterm delivery, to allow immediate paediatric assessment
exp: Clamping is only brought forward when the baby needs resuscitation; otherwise delayed clamping is recommended, including in preterm births.

opts: Anaphylactoid syndrome of pregnancy, about 1 in 100,000 deliveries
Sheehan syndrome, occurring in about 1 in 1,000 deliveries
HELLP syndrome, occurring in about 1 in 10,000 deliveries
Mendelson syndrome, occurring in about 1 in 500 deliveries
exp: Amniotic fluid embolism is also called anaphylactoid syndrome of pregnancy; it is rare at about 1 in 100,000 but catastrophic.

q: Outcome of posterior rotation — anthropoid pelvis : other pelvis types.
opts: Anthropoid: face-to-pubes delivery — other pelvis: deep sacral arrest with the head stuck
Anthropoid: deep sacral arrest — other pelvis: face-to-pubes delivery
Both pelves end in a face-to-pubes delivery after posterior rotation
Both pelves require caesarean section once rotation has gone posterior
exp: The long antero-posterior diameter of the anthropoid pelvis permits face-to-pubes delivery; in other pelves the head arrests deeply.

opts: Retained products: a thick vascular endometrium — remodelling: tubular hypoechoic areas in the myometrium
Retained products: a thin endometrium — remodelling: a uniformly small uterus
Retained products: free fluid in the pouch — remodelling: an adnexal mass
Retained products: an empty cavity — remodelling: a thick endometrium
exp: Retained products show as a thickened vascular endometrium, while a remodelling defect shows tubular hypoechoic spaces in the myometrium.

opts: HIV on treatment, COVID-19, mastitis, and hepatitis B positivity once the baby is immunised
Classic galactosaemia in the infant, which is an absolute contraindication
Untreated active pulmonary tuberculosis in the mother
An active herpes lesion on the breast itself
exp: Breastfeeding continues in treated HIV, COVID-19 and mastitis, and in hepatitis B carriers once the infant has received immunoglobulin and vaccine.
